# Hash-pinned install set for the pip + wheel bootstrap step.
#
# Direct requirements: pip wheel
#
# The three desktop bundle jobs (macOS, Windows, Linux) open with
# `pip install --upgrade pip wheel`. That is the same bootstrap pinned in
# pip-bootstrap.txt, plus `wheel`, which those jobs need because
# desktop/requirements-dev.txt pulls PyGObject, an sdist-only build on Linux.
# An unpinned resolve there means the tool assembling the bundle's native
# dependencies was whatever PyPI served that minute -- and then that pip
# verifies every hash below it.
#
# Deliberately a THIRD file rather than folding `wheel` into
# pip-bootstrap.txt or reusing pip-build-bootstrap.txt:
#   * pip-bootstrap.txt serves ten call sites that do not build anything;
#     three of them bootstrap a throwaway venv to prove a freshly installed
#     wheel boots on its own, and widening those venvs is exactly the bug an
#     isolated-venv test exists to catch.
#   * pip-build-bootstrap.txt carries PyPA `build`, which these jobs never
#     invoke -- they bundle with PyInstaller, not a wheel build -- and its
#     header notes it omits `colorama`, so it cannot serve a Windows job
#     without a change. One of the three call sites here IS windows-latest.
# Keeping the sets apart keeps every job's installed set identical to what it
# was before this pin.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash. Every transitive dependency
# is present because --require-hashes demands the whole closure; `packaging`
# is wheel's (wheel 0.48.0 declares `packaging>=24.0`), not padding.
#
# No platform-conditional dependency is omitted: unlike `build`, neither
# `wheel` nor `packaging` declares an environment-marked requirement, so the
# same closure resolves on all three runners this file serves.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (wheels for each platform, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that
# matches any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the runner
# resolving to the same wheel this file was generated against. That is what
# lets one file serve the macos/windows/ubuntu matrix here.
#
# pip 26.x requires Python >= 3.10. All three call sites pin
# `python-version: "3.11"`.
#
# Updating: Dependabot owns the routine bumps (see the /.github/requirements
# pip entry in .github/dependabot.yml) and rewrites the hashes with them. A
# pin with no updater is the frozen end of the same problem an unpinned
# install is at the other end of.
#
# Regenerating by hand, on Linux / CPython 3.11 to match the job:
#   pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --report r.json pip wheel
# then, for each resolved name==version, take every sha256 under `urls` in
# https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json.

packaging==26.3 \
    --hash=sha256:d7193f7c8e4e93f444fde0262bf90af30e16fa0ad0ad44cb553c87339b23cd1c \
    --hash=sha256:94edc256424af38762eb31306eed28beb9f0efc50a8837492c9d6fd6004aed79
pip==26.2.1 \
    --hash=sha256:71138adf1f4ca900cdb7d289c21b7494329f2332b6d85f0e1c42108c0384ed3e \
    --hash=sha256:f6ad667e89a1fe78046c8f13232b247200f5258d7828f3f7883d660878e0813f
wheel==0.48.0 \
    --hash=sha256:3217dcc807155e45db462d7ef2431f5ddda0d7273b700d05a67b271ceb1287ab \
    --hash=sha256:94800765601e9171bf5d58d066e640662842bcedcbab982b2c90787a2c987322
